newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - S.African gold mines' rich Q4 now history.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - S.African gold mines' rich Q4 now history.

text.p: South African gold mines should report December quarter earnings up nine to 13 percent on the previous quarter, benefitting from fewer holidays and a richer rand gold price.
But the outlook for 1997 is grim with revenues in the March quarter likely to be hit hard by bullion's meltdown and production pressured by four public holidays.

"My expectations for this fourth quarter in general are that we are going to be pleasantly surprised by the figures...but unfortunately that doesn't really hold for the rest of the year, or for the next quarter anyway," Dave Giese, analyst at Smith Borkum Hare, told Reuters.
"The fourth quarter gold price was quite a lot better than it is now."
Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd kicks off the December quarter round of gold results reporting on Thursday.

When the rand shed 29 percent of its value against the dollar in 1996, it carried the local currency gold price to record levels, pushing it above 1,800 rand an ounce at the end of October and buoying mine earnings in the last three months of 1996.
But bullion's recent punishment at the hands of investment funds and speculators, combined with a steadier rand, seems to have eroded any further gains in this current March quarter.
The bullion price lost $15 in the first few days of 1997, sliding to a 3-1/2 year low below $354 an ounce on Thursday.
It was last back above $358 an ounce and had dragged the rand gold price to around 1,672 rand an ounce.
Analysts said that the December quarter's reporting would hopefully shed light on the gold mines' chances for improved efficiency and productivity in 1997.

"What I'm hoping to hear is that people are looking carefully at their productivity. Especially in view of the current gold price we're going to have to get more efficient," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

He added that the softer bullion price could also force certain South African producers to sell a bit more production forward to lock in a safe price in the short-term in order to protect projects already underway.
"We might see some short-term forward selling just to protect. I don't anticipate the guys going into it long term."
Analysts said fewer shifts worked in the current quarter would raise unit working costs, which, combined with the weak bullion price, could hack about 100 rand an ounce off profits.

Still, the December quarter was unlikely to disappoint as the industry should have earned on average over those three months 1,720 rand per ounce for any gold sold at spot, said Nick Goodwin, analyst at Fedsure Asset Management.
After tax and capital spending, the total industry's earnings could jump to around 680 million rand from 610 million rand in the previous quarter, he added.

Furthermore, with only December figures still outstanding, gold production in the fourth quarter was likely to have risen to about 124 tonnes from the approximate 118 tonnes in the third quarter, which suffered labour unrest and halted production.
"But there (124 tonnes) it will stabilise. We won't see a huge revivial in gold production," Goodwin added.
The industry produced 450.6 tonnes of gold in the 11 months to end-November.
Analysts have recently said that 1996's gold output -- expected to be between 490 and 495 tonnes -- while being the lowest in 40 years, would also be the end of the decline.

"We might have another year of similar production, but we are about to enter a period where (certain expansion projects) will be increasing production so this trend will reverse and we will see an improvement in about a year or so," Giese said.
Gold mines expected to stage a particularly strong December quarter performance include Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd and HJ Joel Gold Mining Co Ltd.
